summary.intent: Use the GSD manager dashboard to drive milestone v2.0 (22 phases, 19 complete) through its remaining phases 76, 78, 79 — dispatching plan/execute/verify as parallel background worktree agents while discussing phase 78 inline — and begin shipping completed phases.
summary.outcome: Phases 76 and 79 were fully planned, executed (surviving a mid-run API quota interruption via resume-in-place), and formally verified (both MET/PASS) with their branches pushed to origin; Phase 76's ship pipeline was dispatched in the background. Phase 78 was discussed inline, locking three key decisions (web vitest CI scope, download progress UI wiring, and an infra-independent recovery-tool crypto design), and its CONTEXT.md/DISCUSSION-LOG.md were committed to a new feat/78 branch.

repo: The GSD commit helper's phase_branch_template (feat/{slug}) is applied inconsistently: Phase 79's planner auto-switched from its ephemeral worktree-agent-* branch to the canonical feat/{slug} branch on first commit, but Phase 76's planner did not — it stayed on worktree-agent-a5c21ab277e6cead2, requiring manual re-homing (create canonical branch at that commit, push).

EnterWorktree refuses a repo-root→worktree switch on this host, and each Bash call resets cwd to repo root — background agents must drive worktree work via absolute paths / `git -C` instead, which also means the formal gsd-verifier/phase-level verification pass gets skipped when execute runs this way (had to be dispatched separately afterward).

The ship-phase pipeline (verify→secure→crypto-review→security-review→validate→simplify→SDK E2E gate→CodeRabbit→reword→open PR→resolve threads→extract learnings) is much heavier than execute-phase; its SDK E2E gate resets shared Postgres+Kubo state and binds the API on :3000, so it cannot run twice concurrently — ship must be serialized across phases even when execute was parallelized.
apps/web vitest picks up only `*.test.ts`; `.spec.ts` files are silently skipped — relevant to any 'wire X into CI' decision for web tests.

Recovery tool v3 must be trust-nothing/infra-independent: the SDK's read chain routes IPNS resolve + IPFS fetch through the CipherBox API, so it cannot be used; must reuse packages/crypto + packages/core directly with a standalone IPNS/IPFS walk over a configurable HTTP gateway, keyed only off the user-supplied privateKey.

Folder identity is intentionally ipnsName-keyed, not Node.id-keyed — a ROADMAP scope item implying re-keying to Node.id was proven wrong by research (reintroduces a known orphaned-store bug) and correctly treated as a stale-comment deletion, not a re-key, in Phase 79's plans.
ipns@10.1.3's `IPNSRecord.validity` is an RFC3339 string, not a `Date` as a Phase 76 plan assumed — required mapping via `new Date(record.validity)`.

code.finding: recover_root_keys_from_key_blob ECIES-unwraps the ORIGINAL root keys during vault-init retry; initialize_vault mints fresh random root keys each call, so retry logic must decrypt-and-resume, never re-mint.
Global FP-resolve cycle_budget computed as MAX_CONCURRENT_FP_RESOLVES.saturating_sub(resolving_file_pointers.len()), feeding both loops — fixes a cross-cycle cap that previously wasn't global.
createdAt made a mandatory number field on ResolvedChild, mirroring modifiedAt.
resolveChildren() populates the new mandatory createdAt from Node.createdAt.
collectDescendantFolderIds implemented as a parentId-walking BFS (not a Node.id re-key) for recursive folder-delete cleanup, preserving ipnsName-keyed identity.

workflow: When background agents commit atomically per-plan, a mid-run API/session quota kill can be resumed in-place by inspecting the phase branch for completed vs. in-flight (no-SUMMARY) commits and any uncommitted worktree diffs, rather than restarting from scratch — preserves installed deps (node_modules) and partial progress.

Two heavy parallel background executors running full test suites (cargo + vitest) is what exhausted the session/API quota, not just RAM — worth defaulting to fewer concurrent heavy agents or explicitly asking the user before re-parallelizing after a quota hit.

Discuss-phase adds little value when a phase's scope is already pinned down by explicit source todos with named functions/behaviors — skipping discuss and going straight to plan is reasonable in that case, deferring gray-area elicitation to the planner's research pass.

friction: Both Phase 76 and Phase 79 background executors were killed simultaneously mid-run by an API session-limit hit (reset 12:40am Europe/Berlin), losing live progress until resumed from atomic commits.

EnterWorktree's refusal to switch from repo-root into an existing worktree forced agents into inline absolute-path/git -C workarounds, which in turn caused the formal per-phase gsd-verifier pass to be skipped during execute and need a separate follow-up dispatch.

Phase 76's planner committed to the wrong (ephemeral) branch while Phase 79's planner correctly landed on the canonical phase branch — inconsistent behavior required manual verification and re-homing work before either could be pushed.
Had to manually free phase branches from stale planner worktrees (worktree remove) before executors could check them out cleanly.
open_items: Phase 76 has an open blocking Windows CI merge gate: the D-07 winfsp code landed but can't compile on macOS, so Cargo Check & Test (Windows) + Desktop E2E (windows-latest) must go green on the PR before merge.

Phase 79's ship-phase pipeline (PR, CodeRabbit, security/crypto review, etc.) has not yet been dispatched — deferred until Phase 76's ship completes because the SDK E2E gate can't run concurrently for both.
Phase 78 is discussed (CONTEXT.md + DISCUSSION-LOG.md committed to feat/78) but not yet planned, executed, or verified — the last of the 22 phases without a plan.
Phase 79's 76-style formal gsd-verifier pass was actually run and passed after the transcript's earlier 'optional' framing — worth confirming this is reflected consistently in STATE.md/dashboard.

Backlog scope deferred during Phase 78 discuss: only todo items 3 (poll-monotonicity) and 11 (descent-vs-restore race) were locked in for fix-with-e2e-coverage; the rest of the 68.2/73 backlog items were explicitly deferred per roadmap default.
invite.service.ts:284 remains an explicitly unresolved decision in Phase 79 (no ResolvedChild in scope) rather than a mechanical .kind read — flagged for execute-time attention, now shipped as-is.
